institutional_change: Christian communities became legally recognized corporate recipients of buildings and other property.
evidence: Lactantius preserves the letter ordering places of assembly and property belonging to churches restored without payment.
limits: A legal order does not measure how fully restitution occurred or how many people were Christian.

institutional_change: An emperor used imperial summons and presence to help a church-wide council deliberate and circulate a creed.
evidence: Eusebius describes Constantine convoking the council and addressing its assembled bishops.
limits: Nicaea did not end Christian disagreement and council attendance is not a population census.

institutional_change: Imperial law explicitly prescribed the faith associated with Damasus of Rome and Peter of Alexandria.
evidence: Codex Theodosianus 16.1.2 preserves the edict Cunctos populos issued by Theodosius I with Gratian and Valentinian II.
limits: A law names an official norm; it does not measure belief enforcement or compliance across the empire.
